obligate_myrmecophile.basisOfRecord_reasoning: The classification of an ant association as obligate or facultative is based on observing the ecological behavior and life history traits of the butterfly (e.g., early stages being continually accompanied by ants, females ovipositing only in the presence of host ants, or classification as ant-parasitic nest-inquiline species). These are behavioral and ecological traits observed in nature, fitting the definition of HumanObservation.
obligate_myrmecophile.measurementMethod: Scoring based on observed ecological behaviors and life history traits: Butterflies are scored as obligate myrmecophiles if their early stages are (almost) continually accompanied by ants, often with larger numbers of worker ants around, and especially if the females are known to oviposit only in the presence of their host ants. Ant-parasitic nest-inquiline lycaenid species are also classified as obligate myrmecophiles. All other butterfly species with ant associations are categorized as facultative myrmecophiles.
obligate_myrmecophile.measurementMethod_reasoning: The method is a qualitative scoring protocol used to determine the nature of the ant association (obligate vs. facultative) for each butterfly species, based on specific criteria related to the observed behavior and life cycle of the butterfly.
